title: Build a Web Scraper in Go
description: Build a concurrent web crawler with URL handling, local HTML fixtures, bounded traversal, and deterministic reports.

lessons.title: Welcome
lessons.instruction: A crawler repeats a small pipeline: normalize a URL, fetch it, extract new URLs, then report what it found. Put those stages in execution order.

lessons.title: Golang Setup
lessons.instruction: Reuse one http.Client for connection pooling and give it a timeout; the zero timeout can wait forever. Configure this client to stop after five seconds.

lessons.title: Normalize URLs
lessons.instruction: Resolve relative references against the page URL before deduplication. Fragments do not identify a different document, and host names are case-insensitive; remove the fragment and lowercase the host.

lessons.title: Extract Page Content
lessons.instruction: Visible page content excludes markup plus script and style text. This local fixture is valid XHTML so the standard XML tokenizer is enough here; real websites need a tolerant HTML tokenizer.

lessons.title: Extract Links and Images
lessons.instruction: Links and image sources may be relative. Resolve href and src values against the page URL, discard non-HTTP schemes, and clear fragments before adding them to the crawl frontier.

lessons.title: Structure Page Data
lessons.instruction: A typed page record keeps extraction and reporting separate. Add JSON field names so the exported report has the lowercase keys consumers expect.

lessons.title: Main
lessons.instruction: Keep command-line parsing separate from crawling so it is easy to test. Parse one seed URL plus the maximum page count, request timeout, and report path from the supplied arguments.

lessons.title: Get HTML
lessons.instruction: A fetch helper must close the response body, accept only successful HTML responses, and cap how much it reads. Fetch this local test server without touching the public network.

lessons.title: Adding Recursion
lessons.instruction: Pages can link back to ancestors, so mark a URL visited before following its outgoing links. Complete the traversal so the cyclic local site graph visits each page once.

lessons.title: Concurrency
lessons.instruction: A fixed worker pool bounds simultaneous fetches and avoids one goroutine per discovered URL. Start two workers, feed them the local paths, and sort results before reporting so output stays deterministic.

lessons.title: Max Pages
lessons.instruction: Reserve a page slot before fetching it. The duplicate check, limit check, and reservation must share one lock so concurrent workers cannot admit the same URL or exceed the maximum.

lessons.title: JSON Report
lessons.instruction: Concurrent crawls discover pages in an unpredictable order. Sort records by URL before JSON encoding so reports, diffs, and tests remain stable.

lessons.title: Submit the Link to Your Repository!
lessons.instruction: A shareable crawler needs safe defaults, tests, usage instructions, and a reproducible JSON report. Complete the final readiness check for the project configuration represented here.
